passage: In the village, the results were pasted on the panchayat wall, and Rajni's name was among those who had failed maths. At home her Dilnaz Chachi said loudly, "Look at how your cousin passed with first division." Papa said nothing all evening and ate with his eyes on the plate. Rajni went to the cattle shed and sat with the calf until dark, feeling smaller with every hour. Early next morning Dilnaz Chachi found her there and sat beside her. "I spoke wrongly last night. Tea first. We'll talk about the supplementary exam later. And if this heavy feeling doesn't lift, we'll go to the school counsellor together." Rajni began to cry, and it eased a little.

qa.q: Where did Rajni sit until dark?
qa.a: Rajni sat in the cattle shed with the calf.

qa.q: How did Rajni feel after the comparison and Papa's silence?
qa.a: Ashamed, feeling smaller with every hour.

qa.q: What did Dilnaz Chachi do the next morning that helped?
qa.a: She sat beside Rajni, admitted she spoke wrongly, offered tea first and talk of the supplementary exam later, and mentioned the school counsellor.

qa.q: What might Dilnaz Chachi have realised overnight?
qa.a: That the loud comparison had hurt Rajni, so support should come first and discussion later.

grounding: Shows a student who failed hearing comparison and silence at home and feeling more ashamed until support comes before discussion.

passage: Oskar handed the failed chemistry test to his mother Mina at the kitchen table. Mina read it, said nothing, and turned off the stove with a click. The silence stretched. "Say something," Oskar said. "I don't know what to say yet," Mina answered, and left the room. Oskar heard his sister whispering on the phone. He felt like a stain on the family. An hour later Mina came back, put a hand on his shoulder and said, "I was shocked and I needed a minute. I'm not angry with you. Let's eat, and tomorrow we'll look at what happened." The next day they met the school counsellor. Oskar still felt low, but not alone.

qa.q: Which test did Oskar fail?
qa.a: Oskar failed the chemistry test.

qa.q: What did Oskar feel during the silence?
qa.a: Ashamed and lonely, like a stain on the family.

qa.q: What did Mina do after taking a minute?
qa.a: Mina came back, put a hand on Oskar's shoulder, said she was not angry, and planned to look at what happened after a meal, including a meeting with the school counsellor.

qa.q: Why did Mina leave the room?
qa.a: Mina was shocked and needed a minute before responding.

grounding: Shows a student who failed hearing heavy silence at home and feeling ashamed until a parent offers support first and next steps later.

passage:
School counsellor's note, Thursday.
Ojas came to my room at lunch, sent by his class teacher, who noticed he had stopped eating in the canteen. He failed two subjects in the half-yearly exams.
He told me that at home his father shouted for a long time, then said, "Anirban scored ninety in everything. What is wrong with you?" Anirban is his cousin, the same age. Since then, Ojas said, nobody at home talks to him at dinner. "It's worse than the shouting."
He kept his eyes on the floor. He said he feels stupid and like a disappointment. He did not speak of wanting to harm himself when I asked directly.
I called his parents and asked them to come in this afternoon. They came at four. I explained that Ojas needs support first, and study plans later, and that comparison deepens shame. His mother cried. His father was quiet, then asked, "What should we do tonight?"
We made a small plan. I will see Ojas again on Monday.
— School counsellor

qa.q: Who is Anirban?
qa.a: Anirban is his cousin, the same age.

qa.q: How does Ojas feel about the silence at dinner?
qa.a: Ojas feels ashamed and hurt, saying the silence is worse than the shouting and that he feels like a disappointment.

qa.q: What did the counsellor do that same day, and why was it important?
qa.a: The counsellor called the parents in that afternoon and explained that support comes first and comparison deepens shame, so home could change that night.

qa.q: How might Ojas's father feel when he asks, "What should we do tonight?"
qa.a: His father probably feels shaken and unsure, realising his anger and comparison had hurt Ojas, and wanting to do better.

grounding: Illustrates a student who failed and meets anger, comparison and silence at home, and a counsellor who helps the family offer support first.

passage:
Dear Diary,
Chemistry result came. I failed. 21 out of 70.
At home nobody shouted. That was worse. Baba read the message, put his phone face down and went to the balcony. Ma kept cooking and didn't look at me. Dinner was only the sound of spoons. I felt like I had brought something dirty into the house.
I went to my room and didn't come out.
At ten, Thamma knocked. Manjula Thamma never knocks, she just walks in. She sat on my bed with a bowl of payesh. "Bidisha, eat first. Talk later." I ate. Then I cried into her sari for a while.
She said, "Your Baba failed his first year of college. Nobody told you that, na?" I stared at her.
She said we'll talk about tuitions and retests next week, not tonight. Tonight I just have to sleep.
I think I can.

qa.q: What did Bidisha score in chemistry?
qa.a: 21 out of 70.

qa.q: How did Bidisha feel during the silent dinner?
qa.a: Bidisha felt deeply ashamed, as if something dirty had been brought into the house.

qa.q: What did Thamma do that helped, and in what order?
qa.a: Thamma gave comfort first, food and a hug and a story about Baba's own failure, and left talk of tuitions and retests for next week.

qa.q: How might Baba have felt, going out to the balcony?
qa.a: Baba was probably disappointed and upset, and perhaps did not know what to say, but his silence felt like rejection to Bidisha.

grounding: Shows a student who failed and meets heavy silence at home, and a grandmother who offers support first and next steps later.

passage:
Chaitanya: Vidya didi, can I talk?
Vidya: Always. What's up?
Chaitanya: I failed the maths term exam
Chaitanya: Papa said "Why can't you be like Vidya? She never failed anything"
Vidya: Oh Chaitu. I'm so sorry.
Vidya: For the record, I failed Class 9 science. Nobody talks about it.
Chaitanya: seriously?
Vidya: Seriously. I cried for three days.
Chaitanya: I feel like I'm just the stupid one in the family
Vidya: You're not. You're someone who had one bad exam and a painful evening.
Vidya: Have you eaten?
Chaitanya: no
Vidya: Eat something now. Tomorrow, can you talk to the school counsellor? And tonight I'm calling Masi to tell her you need a hug, not a lecture. Okay?
Chaitanya: ok. thanks didi 🤍
Vidya: Next week we'll look at maths together. Not tonight.

qa.q: What did Papa say to Chaitanya?
qa.a: "Why can't you be like Vidya? She never failed anything."

qa.q: How does Chaitanya feel after Papa's comparison?
qa.a: Chaitanya feels ashamed and small, like the stupid one in the family.

qa.q: What does Vidya do that puts support before next steps?
qa.a: Vidya shares her own failure, tells Chaitanya to eat, calls Masi that night to ask for a hug not a lecture, and suggests the counsellor, leaving maths for next week.

qa.q: How might Vidya feel about being used as the comparison?
qa.a: Vidya seems uncomfortable and sad about it, which is why she quickly reveals her own Class 9 failure.

grounding: Illustrates a student who is compared to a cousin after failing, and a cousin who offers support first, involves a parent and suggests a counsellor.

passage:
In Kumbakonam the results were pinned outside the school gate by nine. Karthik read his roll number twice, then walked home the long way, past the temple tank.
His father was waiting on the thinnai. "Trisha scored ninety-two. Your own cousin, same school, same teachers. What were you doing all year?"
His mother said nothing at all. She served dinner and cleared it in silence. The quiet was worse than the shouting.
For a week Karthik stayed in his room, skipped meals, and stopped answering his friends. On the eighth day he told his Periamma, "There's no point trying anything now."
Periamma sat down beside him right then. "You failed an exam. You didn't fail at being my boy." That afternoon she walked him to the school counsellor, Mrs Selvi, and waited outside. Walking home, she said, "We'll talk about the retest next week. Today, just eat with me."

qa.q: What did Karthik's father say Trisha scored?
qa.a: Trisha scored ninety-two.

qa.q: How did the comparison and the silence at home make Karthik feel?
qa.a: They left him more ashamed and hopeless, so he hid in his room, skipped meals and said there was no point trying.

qa.q: What did Periamma do that helped?
qa.a: Periamma comforted him first, said failing an exam was not failing as a person, took him to the counsellor that same afternoon, and left retest plans for later.

qa.q: What would change if Karthik's father had spoken to him the way Periamma did?
qa.a: Karthik might have felt supported instead of ashamed, and might not have shut himself away for a week.

grounding: Shows a student who failed meeting comparison and heavy silence at home, then support first and a counsellor's help.
